title: Building a Flock from Three Local Rules
concept_layer: swarm intelligence; Reynolds' boids (separation, alignment, cohesion); local rules → collective behavior; coordination without centralization
domain_deferred: multi-species flock dynamics → later swarm maps

capture_leaks.homogeneous_agents: Every boid has identical weights and perception. Heterogeneous swarms (leaders, roles) emerge differently.
capture_leaks.euclidean_perception: Boids see any neighbor within radius regardless of direction. Real animals have visual cones; blind spots matter.
capture_leaks.no_memory: Each boid acts purely on current neighbor state. Memory (past positions, learned routes) requires state per agent — deferred to ML.
capture_leaks.no_energy_or_hunger: Boids never tire, don’t need food, don’t die. Ecosystem-level dynamics (predation, starvation, reproduction) need agent-based modeling (ABM) which sibling artifacts cover.
capture_leaks.newtonian_physics_only: Steering + velocity + position. No flocking-through-fluid (drag varies), no quantum-like correlation, no signal delay. Real biological swarms (starlings) have astonishing low-latency — Reynolds boids are an approximation.

limit: Fifty particles, three rules, one flock. The artifact captures that coordination is not agreement — it is geometry. A boid doesn’t decide to join the flock; it is IN the flock by virtue of neighbor relations. What it refuses: hierarchy, memory, energetics, heterogeneity. Each is a door that later swarm or ML maps open.

grammar_alignment.note: boid_manager teaches 'flock' — the foundational swarm operation with three local rules. Other swarm operations are specialized: stigmergy replaces direct perception with trail-reading; physarum uses slime-mold rules; PSO optimizes a function via swarm dynamics. All are variations of local-rules → collective.

biome_alignment.note: Biome density 0.9 — the world is near-fully alive. Creatures now exhibit flocking behavior naturally. The player’s 'disturb_swarm' verb lets them reach into any swarm and watch it reform around their arm. The 'swarm' catalyst turns solo creatures into collectives.

stages.title: From soft body to social body
stages.thinking: SoftBodies_Soft_Body_Deformation taught that matter is a spring-mass lattice — vertices connected by springs that respond to force. What if we take the lattice apart? Each vertex becomes an independent agent, each spring becomes a RULE rather than a constraint. Boids are a soft body dissolved into social agents. The same neighbor-coupling logic, but now each agent DECIDES based on its neighbors instead of being mechanically tied to them.
stages.code:
# SoftBody: vertex_i.position mechanically constrained by springs to neighbors
# Boid:     agent_i.velocity deliberately steered based on neighbor state
#
# The shift:
#   MECHANICAL constraint → BEHAVIORAL rule
#   rest-length springs → alignment/cohesion/separation
#   involuntary → voluntary (each agent is the agent of its motion)
#
# Social physics.
# The spring-mass graph is still there — but now each node chooses.

stages.title: Reynolds' three rules (1987)
stages.thinking: Craig Reynolds defined three rules for each boid: SEPARATION (steer away from neighbors that are too close), ALIGNMENT (match neighbor heading), COHESION (steer toward neighbor center). Each rule is a local computation — the boid looks only at neighbors within perception radius. The three vectors are weighted and summed into a steering force. From these three rules: birds, fish, bats. From these three rules: traffic, crowds, markets. From these three rules: much of collective behavior.

stages.title: Each boid is a mover with a perception radius
stages.thinking: A boid is conceptually simple: position, velocity, acceleration (the Mover pattern from ForcesFoundations). What’s new is perception: every frame, the boid finds all neighbors within radius r. That neighbor list feeds the three rules. The perception radius is THE critical parameter. Too small: each boid is alone (no flock). Too large: every boid averages the entire population (no flock, just slow drift toward the center). Between the two extremes: flocking emerges.

stages.title: Spawn many in a volume
stages.thinking: BoidManager spawns 50 boids in a 20×10×20 volume. Positions are randomized. Initial velocities are small random vectors. Within a few seconds, the rules take over: clumps form, clumps align, clumps merge into a flock. The manager owns the boid array and calls update() on each per frame. Nothing coordinates them centrally — all coordination emerges.

stages.title: The VR hand as attractor/repulsor
stages.thinking: Left trigger: boids steer toward controller. Right trigger: boids steer away. Your hand becomes an invisible presence — a boulder in a river. Reach into the flock: it parts around your arm. Pull back: it reforms. This is the moment the artifact becomes unforgettable. Abstract emergence becomes embodied relation. You are a boid that happens to be bigger and smarter than the others, temporarily steering them.

stages.title: Tune the weights — find different flocks
stages.thinking: Separation, alignment, cohesion each have a weight. Different weight combinations produce different swarm personalities. Heavy separation, light cohesion: particle cloud, barely coheres. Balanced: recognizable flock. Heavy alignment: stream of agents all moving in parallel. Heavy cohesion: clump that tries to collapse into a point. The three-weight space is a parameter atlas of flocking styles. Starlings occupy a specific region; bees occupy another.
stages.code:
@export_range(0.0, 3.0, 0.1) var separation_weight: float = 1.5
@export_range(0.0, 3.0, 0.1) var alignment_weight: float = 1.0
@export_range(0.0, 3.0, 0.1) var cohesion_weight: float = 1.0

# Different regimes:
#   (high, low, low)  → anti-social particle gas
#   (1.5, 1.0, 1.0)   → starling-like flock (default)
#   (low, high, high) → dense column, moves as a snake
#   (low, low, high)  → collapsing blob, ends as a point
#   (low, high, low)  → parallel streams, no aggregation
#
# Same three rules. Infinite collective behaviors.

stages.title: Wall wrap or bounce — boundary conditions matter
stages.thinking: The boids live in a finite box. When they hit a wall: either wrap (toroidal world) or bounce (reflection) or get repelled (soft boundary). Each choice changes long-run behavior. Wrap: a boid leaving the right comes in the left, creating infinite-world illusion. Bounce: boids accumulate near walls, creating eddies. Repel: keeps flock centered. The artifact uses a soft repulsion to keep the flock visible. Boundary conditions are not trivia; they are half the physics.
stages.code:
@export var bounds_size = Vector3(20, 10, 20)
@export var boundary_strength = 5.0

func _apply_boundary(b: Boid) -> void:
	var half = bounds_size * 0.5
	var repulsion = Vector3.ZERO
	
	if b.position.x > half.x:  repulsion.x -= boundary_strength
	if b.position.x < -half.x: repulsion.x += boundary_strength
	if b.position.y > half.y:  repulsion.y -= boundary_strength
	if b.position.y < -half.y: repulsion.y += boundary_strength
	if b.position.z > half.z:  repulsion.z -= boundary_strength
	if b.position.z < -half.z: repulsion.z += boundary_strength
	
	b.acceleration += repulsion

# Soft repulsion:
#   - boids don't bounce off walls (unrealistic)
#   - they gently redirect as they approach (natural)
#   - this encourages flock to stay central without hard boundaries

stages.title: Give it identity
stages.thinking: The boid manager knows what it is. Not a flock simulator — a DEMONSTRATION that coordination is geometry. No boid knows the flock exists. No rule mentions 'stay together.' Yet the flock emerges and holds together and bends around obstacles and reforms around your hand. Because each agent does three small things with its neighbors, the collective does amazing things none of them can name. The critical parameter is interaction_radius because perception IS the flock. Below a threshold: dust. Above: a body with no skin.
stages.code:
# @identity
# essence: f_i = Σ(neighbor_j)[separate(i,j) + align(vel_j) + cohere(pos_j)] — three weighted averages over a local neighborhood
# desire: to reach out a VR hand and feel the flock split and reform around your arm — to be a boulder in a river of agency
# critical_parameter: interaction_radius — at zero, it's a particle cloud; past a threshold, a coherent organism crystallizes from the randomness
# triggers: left trigger attracts boids toward controller; right trigger repels — learner's body becomes a temporary leader with no followers bound by loyalty
# emerges: coordinated lane reversals, vortex rings, and split-rejoin events that no rule specifies — the flock invents maneuvers

# truth: coordination is not agreement — it is geometry; close enough means you are already the same
